title: A Book of Nonsense
author: Edward Lear
text:
R was a rabbit,
Who had a bad habit
Of eating the flowers
In gardens and bowers.
r
Naughty fat rabbit!
question: Why is the rabbit considered naughty?
options: It makes too much noise.
It eats flowers in gardens.
It runs away from home.
explanation: Правильный ответ: 'Of eating the flowers / In gardens and bowers.' Кролик ел цветы в садах.

text:
A lonely young ghost in a hall,
Decided to go to the mall.
He bought some bright jeans,
To fit in with teens,
And walked right straight through a brick wall.
question: Why did the ghost buy bright jeans?
options: To stay warm in the mall
To look like the teenagers
To match his invisible wall
explanation: В тексте сказано: «To fit in with teens» (чтобы быть своими среди подростков).

title: Jeeves Stories
author: P. G. Wodehouse
text: It must have been about one in the afternoon when I woke. I was feeling more or less like something the Pure Food Committee had rejected, but there was one bright thought which cheered me up, and that was that about now the twins would be leaning on the rail of the liner, taking their last glimpse of the dear old homeland.
question: Why was Bertie feeling happy when he woke up?
options: He believed the twins had already left for South Africa.
He was looking forward to eating eggs and bacon.
He had just enjoyed a wonderful and refreshing sleep.
explanation: Правильный ответ: первая мысль, которая его обрадовала, была о том, что близнецы уже уплывают: 'about now the twins would be leaning on the rail of the liner'.

text: "Why on earth are you wearing running shoes and gym shorts to a fancy restaurant?" asked Clara, looking shocked. "Well, your text clearly said we had to run if we wanted to get a table," Leo replied, wiping sweat from his forehead. "I meant take a quick taxi, not literally sprint across four busy city blocks!" she groaned, covering her face.
question: Why did Leo run all the way to the restaurant?
options: He wanted to exercise before dinner.
He misunderstood Clara's text message.
He couldn't find a taxi in the city.
He forgot his clothes for the evening.
explanation: Лео понял слова буквально: «your text clearly said we had to run», хотя Клара имела в виду такси («I meant take a quick taxi»).

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
text:
Scrooge looked at the Ghost, and, with a mournful shaking of his head, glanced anxiously towards the door.
It opened; and a little girl, much younger than the boy, came darting in, and, putting her arms about his neck, and often kissing him, addressed him as her “dear, dear brother.”
“I have come to bring you home, dear brother!” said the child, clapping her tiny hands, and bending down to laugh. “To bring you home, home, home!”
“Home, little Fan?” returned the boy.
question: Why is the little girl so excited when she arrives?
options: She has run away from her parents.
She has received a Christmas present.
She has come to take her brother home.
explanation: Девочка радостно восклицает: «I have come to bring you home, dear brother!»

title: Indian Fairy Tales
author: Joseph Jacobs
text: When the king’s attendants informed the prince about the death of his father he wept and wailed, and gave notice that he would give half of his kingdom to anyone who should bring him news about the murderer of his father. The goldsmith knew full well that it was a tiger that killed the king, and not any hunter’s hands, since he had heard from Gangazara how he obtained the crown. Still, he resolved to denounce Gangazara as the king’s murderer, so, hiding the crown under his garments, he flew to the palace.
question: Why did the goldsmith accuse Gangazara of the murder?
options: To get the reward promised by the prince
Because the prince forced him to confess
To protect the wild tiger from hunters
Because he believed Gangazara was guilty
explanation: Принц обещал полкоролевства за убийцу, поэтому ювелир оклеветал невиновного: «Still, he resolved to denounce Gangazara as the king’s murderer».

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
text: Her first idea was that she had somehow fallen into the sea, “and in that case I can go back by railway,” she said to herself. (Alice had been to the seaside once in her life, and had come to the general conclusion, that wherever you go to on the English coast you find a number of bathing machines in the sea, some children digging in the sand with wooden spades, then a row of lodging houses, and behind them a railway station.) However, she soon made out that she was in the pool of tears which she had wept when she was nine feet high.
question: Why did Alice think she could go back home by train?
options: She had already bought a return train ticket.
She saw a row of lodging houses near the water.
She frequently visited the seaside by train.
She heard a train moving somewhere nearby.
She believed every English coast had a train station.
explanation: Алиса решила, что на любом побережье есть вокзал: «wherever you go to on the English coast you find... behind them a railway station».

title: Indian Fairy Tales
author: Joseph Jacobs
text:
Looking out, she saw the lad hale and hearty standing before her, and grew whiter than ever with rage and spite.
She sent for him to ask how he had returned so soon, and when she heard how kindly her mother had received him, she very nearly had a fit
question: How did the white Queen feel when she saw the young man alive and well?
options: She was happy to see him again
She was proud of his cleverness
She was confused and asked for help
She was extremely angry and shocked
explanation: Она злилась: "grew whiter than ever with rage and spite... she very nearly had a fit".

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
text:
“Ghost of the Future!” he exclaimed, “I fear you more than any spectre I have seen. But as I know your purpose is to do me good, and as I hope to live to be another man from what I was, I am prepared to bear your company, and do it with a thankful heart. Will you not speak to me?”
It gave him no reply. The hand was pointed straight before them.
question: Why is Scrooge willing to travel with the Ghost?
options: He believes the Ghost will help him change.
He wants to prove how brave he has become.
He is no longer afraid of ghostly spirits.
The Ghost ordered him to follow immediately.
explanation: Скрудж говорит: «...your purpose is to do me good, and as I hope to live to be another man... I am prepared to bear your company».

text:
My phone is dead, my coffee is cold,
And the umbrella gave up in the rain.
I am soaked to the bone and looking old,
Oh, Monday is playing with my brain!
question: What is the mood of this short song?
options: Excited and energetic
Calm and optimistic
Frustrated and dramatic
Bored and sleepy
explanation: Текст полон комичного отчаяния: "Monday is playing with my brain!"

text: Dear Diary, today I stared deeply into the soul of my human while they ate pizza, using my most tragic and starving facial expression. It worked brilliantly, and I got a delicious piece of crust with melted cheese. Honestly, ruling this household requires very little effort when the staff is so easily manipulated.
question: Why did the pet stare at the human?
options: To protect the house
To warn about danger
To get some tasty pizza
explanation: Текст подтверждает это: "I got a delicious piece of crust with melted cheese" после грустного взгляда на пиццу.

text:
Open the fridge, hoping for a snack,
Got no tasty food, only sadness back.
A lonely lemon sits and looks at me,
Staring at the wall like it is sad to see.
Jump to my shoes, running to the shop,
Buying all the chips until I drop!
question: Why does the person leave the house in a hurry?
options: To meet a friend near the local shop
To buy snacks after seeing an empty fridge
To catch a bus before it drives away
To find a lost lemon in the street
explanation: Open the fridge... Buying all the chips until I drop!

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
text: She took down a jar from one of the shelves as she passed; it was labelled “Orange Marmalade,” but to her great disappointment it was empty: she did not like to drop the jar for fear of killing somebody, so managed to put it into one of the cupboards as she fell past it.
question: Why did Alice put the empty jar back into a cupboard?
options: She was afraid of hitting someone below.
She knew the jar was full of jam.
She wanted to keep it for herself.
She wanted to clean the shelves.
explanation: Правильный ответ: she did not like to drop the jar for fear of killing somebody.

title: Indian Fairy Tales
author: Joseph Jacobs
text: This was too much for any farmer to stand; and our friend brooded over it, and brooded over it, till at last a bright idea came into his head. He seized the conch, blew it loudly, and cried out, “Oh, Ram! I wish to be blind of one eye!” And so he was, in a twinkling, but the moneylender of course was blind of both, and in trying to steer his way between the two new wells, he fell into one, and was drowned.
question: Why did the farmer wish to be blind in one eye?
options: He wanted to test the magical power of the conch
To make the greedy moneylender completely blind
To punish himself for being too jealous
He accidentally made a wrong wish in a hurry
He was tired of farming and wanted to rest
explanation: Правильный ответ: „the moneylender of course was blind of both“ — фермер знал правило удваивания и решил пожертвовать глазом ради врага.

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
text: The terrible announcement that the baby had been taken in the act of putting a doll’s frying pan into his mouth, and was more than suspected of having swallowed a fictitious turkey, glued on a wooden platter! The immense relief of finding this a false alarm!
question: What funny emergency happened with the baby?
options: He hid the Christmas presents.
He broke the doll's frying pan.
He fell down the stairs.
He ate a real turkey for dinner.
He nearly swallowed a toy turkey.
explanation: Правильный ответ: baby had been taken in the act of putting a doll’s frying pan into his mouth, and was more than suspected of having swallowed a fictitious turkey

text: The handsome prince finally reached the top tower to wake the sleeping princess with a kiss. Instead of opening her eyes, she sleepily swiped left in the air and mumbled something about blocking annoying strangers. The prince sighed, updated his dating profile, and started climbing down.
question: Why does the prince start climbing down the tower?
options: The princess rejected his kiss online
He forgot his smartphone at the bottom
The princess ignored him in her sleep
He decided to find a better castle
explanation: Она не проснулась, а «sleepily swiped left... and mumbled something about blocking annoying strangers».

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
text: “If any one of them can explain it,” said Alice, (she had grown so large in the last few minutes that she wasn’t a bit afraid of interrupting him,) “I’ll give him sixpence. I don’t believe there’s an atom of meaning in it.”
question: Why is Alice not afraid to interrupt the King?
options: She has a lot of money.
She is the Queen's friend.
She knows the poem's meaning.
She has grown very large.
explanation: В тексте сказано: "she had grown so large in the last few minutes that she wasn't a bit afraid of interrupting him".

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
text:
“You don’t mean to say you took ’em down, rings and all, with him lying there?” said Joe.
“Yes, I do,” replied the woman. “Why not?”
“You were born to make your fortune,” said Joe, “and you’ll certainly do it.”
question: What surprises old Joe about the bed curtains?
options: They were already old and full of holes
They were too heavy for the woman to carry alone
The woman washed them before bringing them in
They are made of very expensive silk material
They were stolen while the dead man was still in bed
explanation: Джо удивляется: «You took 'em down... with him lying there?»

text:
The fridge is dark, the midnight hour is deep.
I came for cheese, while all the world is fast asleep.
Cold light reveals my sad and empty plate.
One lonely carrot sighs and meets its fate.
question: Why is the character eating a carrot in the middle of the night?
options: They are on a strict diet
They hate midnight snacks
There was no cheese left
They love healthy food
explanation: Строка 'Cold light reveals my sad and empty plate' доказывает, что любимого сыра не оказалось.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
text: “The reason is,” said the Gryphon, “that they would go with the lobsters to the dance. So they got thrown out to sea. So they had to fall a long way. So they got their tails fast in their mouths. So they couldn’t get them out again. That’s all.”
question: Why do the whitings have their tails in their mouths according to the Gryphon?
options: They fell into the sea and got stuck.
They are hiding from the porpoise.
They are very hungry and try to eat.
It helps them dance with lobsters.
explanation: Грифон объясняет: «They had to fall a long way. So they got their tails fast in their mouths».

title: Indian Fairy Tales
author: Joseph Jacobs
text: The cat waited till it was quite dark, and then climbed the tree, killed the kite, and recovered the ring. “Come along,” it said to the dog when it reached the ground. “We must make haste now. We have been delayed. Our master will die from grief and suspense. Come on.”
question: Why did the cat and the dog need to hurry back?
options: The bird was flying away again
Their master was dying of grief
It was getting very dark outside
They were afraid of the kite
explanation: Цитата: «Our master will die from grief and suspense.»

text:
Old Joe built a fence so high and wide,
To keep the noisy world outside.
He sat on his porch with a mug of tea,
And smiled at his quiet property.
Then a hungry goat jumped over the wood,
And ate the whole fence for breakfast food.
question: Why did Joe's quiet morning plan fail?
options: A goat ate his fence
His tea got too cold
The wind blew it down
A neighbor yelled at him
explanation: Текст говорит: "And ate the whole fence for breakfast food" — коза съела весь забор Джо.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
text:
“If you didn’t sign it,” said the King, “that only makes the matter worse. You must have meant some mischief, or else you’d have signed your name like an honest man.”
There was a general clapping of hands at this: it was the first really clever thing the King had said that day.
question: How did the people in the courtroom react to the King's words?
options: They got confused by his words.
They clapped and liked his idea.
They laughed at his silly joke.
explanation: «There was a general clapping of hands at this»
